newsitem.title: UK: BHP says UK Lennox oilfield restarted at 10,000 bp.
newsitem.headline: BHP says UK Lennox oilfield restarted at 10,000 bp.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty (BHP) BHP AX said on Monday oil production at its Lennox oilfield west of Britain resumed last week after a year-long shutdown.

Lennox, which delivers crude ashore via the neighbouring Douglas platform, will produce at a restricted rate of 10,000 barrels per day (bpd) for the next three months while commissioning of a new pipeline is completed.
"Oil production from the Douglas reservoirs -- currently running in excess of 50,000 bpd -- will not be affected during this period," BHP said in a statement.

Lennox production was halted last June when a routine inspection revealed faults in a section of the 32-km pipeline which carries gas extracted from the oil at Douglas back to the field for reinjection.
The entire 12-inch diameter pipeline was replaced between last October and March this year.

The partners in the 1.1 billion stg ($1.8 billion) development in Liverpool Bay are operator BHP Petroleum with 46.1 percent, LASMO with 25 percent, Monument with 20 percent and PowerGen North Sea with 8.9 percent.
At full capacity Lennox will pump some 30,000 bpd.
BHP has also installed pipeline heaters to treat the problem of residue build up from the waxy Douglas crude which has hampered the development.
